verses.text: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

xrefs.text: Now when Job’s three friends— Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite— heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.

verses.text: “How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.

xrefs.text: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?

Then the LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD. Behold, the LORD is about to pass by.” And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?”

verses.text: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?

xrefs.text: He is the Rock, His work is perfect; all His ways are just. A God of faithfulness without injustice, righteous and upright is He.

Far be it from You to do such a thing— to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
And now, may the fear of the LORD be upon you. Be careful what you do, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice or partiality or bribery.”
Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.”

verses.text: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.

xrefs.text: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice.
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
because we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.”

verses.text: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,

xrefs.text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,
Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

verses.text: if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.

xrefs.text: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon?
You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies. Awake, my God, and ordain judgment.

verses.text: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.

xrefs.text: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
For who has despised the day of small things? But these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.”
Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.

verses.text: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.

xrefs.text: Remember the days of old; consider the years long past. Ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will inform you.
what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers,

Indeed, ask now from one end of the heavens to the other about the days that long preceded you, from the day that God created man on earth: Has anything as great as this ever happened or been reported?
For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

verses.text: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.

xrefs.text: For we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
My days are like lengthening shadows, and I wither away like grass.
My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.

verses.text: Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?

xrefs.text: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.
The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts. And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead.
Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.

verses.text: Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?

xrefs.text: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
The waters of the Nile will dry up, and the riverbed will be parched and empty.

verses.text: While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass.

xrefs.text: He will be like a shrub in the desert; he will not see when prosperity comes. He will dwell in the parched places of the desert, in a salt land where no one lives.
For, “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,
But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can grow,
The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

verses.text: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.

xrefs.text: The wicked will return to Sheol— all the nations who forget God.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.
For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.

verses.text: His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.

xrefs.text: They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave a spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs will die; crack one open, and a viper is hatched.

verses.text: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.

xrefs.text: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
The wicked man will see and be grieved; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desires of the wicked will perish.
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

verses.text: He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.

xrefs.text: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
The LORD once called you a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit. But with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed.
I have seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree,
I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.

verses.text: His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.

xrefs.text: The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.

Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
Righteous are You, O LORD, when I plead before You. Yet about Your judgments I wish to contend with You: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the faithless live at ease?
As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.

verses.text: If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’

xrefs.text: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
yet he passed away and was no more; though I searched, he could not be found.
The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
Yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more; though you look for them, they will not be found.
Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.

verses.text: Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.

He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dump

He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap. He seats them among princes and bestows on them a throne of honor. For the foundations of the earth are the LORD’s, and upon them He has set the world.
And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father. For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.

Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring the tall tree down and make the low tree tall. I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.’”

verses.text: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.

xrefs.text: Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
Consider the blameless and observe the upright, for posterity awaits the man of peace.
Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand.
This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut:
For the LORD will not forsake His people; He will never abandon His heritage.

verses.text: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.

xrefs.text: Then our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with shouts of joy. Then it was said among the nations, “The LORD has done great things for them.”
Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”
He who goes out weeping, bearing a trail of seed, will surely return with shouts of joy, carrying sheaves of grain.
Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous ones; shout for joy, all you upright in heart.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

verses.text: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”

xrefs.text: I will clothe his enemies with shame, but the crown upon him will gleam.”
May my accusers be clothed with disgrace; may they wear their shame like a robe.
May those who gloat in my distress be ashamed and confounded; may those who exalt themselves over me be clothed in shame and reproach.
He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.
If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’
